reasoning: The extract shows some success measures and monitoring plans, but no testing and no evaluation timetable. Level 1 is clearly reached. The first two lines say the Government wants to develop a way to identify the 'just about managing' group and 'measure their attainment and progress in the school system', and that it will 'work with experts and specialists' to do so. Selective schools would also have to publish information on 'their success in recruiting a fair proportion of below-average income pupils'. Monitoring would run through 'Regional Schools Commissioners and Education Funding Agency and existing data collections' and checks on funding agreement compliance. It would include 'regular visits from DfE education advisers in the first two years'. This outlines how the measures will be developed and gives a monitoring process, which edges toward level 2. However, monitoring compliance with funding agreement requirements is not evaluation of whether the policy worked. The extract has no piloting or testing and no reason why testing is inappropriate. It has no evaluation plan and no outcomes to be assessed, and it has no timetable beyond the two-year visits. It does not say what will happen to results or whether they will be published, other than school website disclosures. The strongest case for level 2 is the process for developing the measure with experts plus the monitoring. That falls short because it lacks testing or evaluation detail. To reach level 2, the document would need to state whether the policy would be piloted or why not, and set out an evaluation of impact on the target group's outcomes. Level 3 would also need reasons, timing and publication plans for results.
